subject: Next steps — GridWorks discovery recap & POC onboarding roadmap

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps — GridWorks discovery recap & POC onboarding roadmap

Hi Casey — great to meet earlier. Short recap from our call and a proposed onboarding roadmap so we have clear owners and next steps. Please reply if anything below is incorrect or missing.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Production transformer for outage/incident classification is inconsistent: 99th pct latency spikes above 1.2s during peak windows.
- Cost per inference and GPU utilization are unpredictable — finance wants unit economics nailed before rollouts.
- Data residency & auditability: logs and KV caches must stay within their VPC; SOC2 evidence required for any hosted component.

Goals for the POC (success criteria)
- Latency: reduce median latency and 95th/99th tail to <250ms for typical alert-size payloads (<=512 tokens).
- Cost: demonstrate >=40% reduction in per-1k-token cost vs current infra under steady QPS.
- Accuracy: maintain or improve current alert classification precision/recall (baseline: 95% precision on labeled test set).
- Throughput: validate sustained 300 QPS with <5% error rate.

Proposed 4-week POC scope
Week 0 (prep): access setup, sample data handoff, baseline metric collection (we will run a short baseline harness against your current endpoint).
Week 1: private deployment of Redwood (VPC) + model variant selection; prefix caching enabled for common alert prefixes.
Week 2: prompt set onboarding and evaluation harness (we'll run automated prompt regressions and build a small prompt example set).
Week 3: load & latency validation, cost analysis, and run-through of failover behavior and model fallback.

Owners and roles
- Commercial/coordination: Jasmine Liu (me) — scheduling, scope changes, procurement touchpoints.
- Technical lead: Vivek Kulkarni — infra, deployment, evals, and on-prem tooling.
- Customer success / onboarding: Monica Patel — runbooks, success metrics, and retention plan.

Immediate asks (action items)
1) Casey: provide SFTP or temporary upload URL for a 10k-sample dataset (anonymized) + current baseline metrics (tail latency, error rates) — target by Tue 5/18.
2) GridWorks IT: create an IAM service account with minimal roles or allow our bootstrap script to create temporary credentials (see Vivek's checklist below).
3) Legal: any required NDAs / DPA pointers — we will not access PII and prefer to proceed under your standard security questionnaires.

Attachments included: gridworks_poc_scope.xlsx (detailed timeline + eval matrix), prompt_examples_v1.jsonl (starter prompt/eval set).

Proposed kickoff: Wed 5/19 10:00am PT — 30 minutes to validate access and confirm the sample dataset format. If that works, Monica will send a calendar invite.

Thanks — excited to get started.

—
Jasmine Liu

Hi Casey — quick technical notes answering your questions and outlining the access approach. Copying the onboarding-checklist.pdf as a stub reference (see attachment).

Access & upload
- We support SFTP to a customer-controlled bastion. Typical flow: GridWorks creates a short-lived SFTP user + home dir; we drop a small bootstrap container (no inbound connections) that pulls data via SFTP using those creds. Alternatively, you can provide a pre-signed S3 link (internal S3 or a signed transfer bucket).
- Max single-file size: 5GB; recommended chunking for >1GB. Total dataset sizes are fine — we stream during ingestion.

Payload sizes & QPS
- The 300 QPS target assumes average alert payload ~200 tokens (text-only). If you have longer payloads (attachments, stack traces), tail latency increases — we'll include a latency-vs-length curve in the baseline report.

Security & auditability
- KV cache and model runtime will be deployed inside your VPC in the POC. We provide access logs, per-request audit IDs, and an audit artifact (JSON) that meets typical SOC2 evidence needs. For anything regulated, we can turn on HSM-backed key encryption if you provide a KMS endpoint.

Eval approach (prompt/eval details)
- We'll run the starter prompt_examples_v1.jsonl you saw as attachment. Proposed evals: precision/recall on the 1k labeled set, latency distribution, and regression checks against a baseline prompt set. We’ll version prompts and store diffed eval results to the Drive folder.

Next steps (technical)
1) Provide SFTP details or a presigned bucket by Tue 5/18.
2) Create an IAM role/service account or allow our bootstrap to use temporary creds; we will rotate creds and provide a short audit before teardown.
3) Confirm whether you want prefix caching enabled for common alert prefixes — this typically reduces token cost by 20–30% for repetitive alerts.

Attachment: onboarding-checklist.pdf (ticket: redwood-onboard-842)

I’ll prepare the baseline harness plan and share it in the Drive folder.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
